says: In next/, desktop.brain-memory is declared with a plain Schema.ByteSize, which accepts "0 B", and a limit of zero replaces the local runtime at every first sample, a restart loop. Fixed in the same pull request: the setting's schema is a byte size above zero, titled "a memory limit" with a description a person reads, so a zero in the person's file fails to load with an invalid settings error that names desktop.brain-memory. A new L9 property in DesktopBrain.test.ts holds it for six spellings of zero.
proof: At 490d3f7a9e40c387808db514281f8adbd293f587, Declarations.ts line 187 is schema: Schema.ByteSize, and ByteSize.isByteSize accepts 0n. The new law, run on that code, fails at its first run: parsing "0 B" succeeds.
cost: A person who writes 0 gets a brain that restarts its runtime every second, with no error at load.
